g.text: else NO_SQL / SQL_PARSE_ERROR (no crash on garbage input)
root must be SELECT/UNION/subquery; reject Insert/Update/Delete/DDL/Command anywhere,
incl. CTE-wrapped DML and multi-statement. READ_ONLY. This is a parser control, not a DB privilege.
every table must be an MDL model; block table-valued functions + denied functions
referenced tables must be in the role's set. ROLE_TABLE_DENIED
expand SELECT * against the schema first, then block PII + denied columns.
Skipped only for roles with can_see_pii. Star-expansion closes the SELECT * leak. CLAC_DENIED
add role's row filter as a sqlglot AST literal (never string concat).
UNION roots wrapped as SELECT * FROM (...) WHERE filter. Injection-safe by construction.

svg.text: only this string is ever sent to a connector's run()
Two residual gaps an auditor should know
PII masking before the LLM matches result column names against the flagged PII list. A privileged (can_see_pii) role whose
SQL aliases a PII column (SELECT email AS contact) produces a name that no longer matches, so real values reach the model.
Non-privileged roles are still protected because CLAC blocks the column reference itself.
PII flagging itself is a column-name substring heuristic. It over-flags (Item_Name) and will miss oddly named identifiers
(account_no, national id) unless an admin curates the list. Document text and memory notes are sent to the model unmasked.
